title: four months of rain
hook: a new king goes to his palace, and the man who made him king goes to a cave
carry: chaturmas, the four holy months of rain

segments.voice: Yesterday: Tara's lament, Vali's last words, and Angada at the pyre. Antyeshti, the last rite, and room to grieve. Today the week closes.

Sugriva is crowned. Angada is named heir. The city celebrates with drums and garlands. And Rama doesn't go in. He's an exile, he says, and he promised fourteen years outside any village or town. So the new king of Kishkindha goes to his palace, and the man who made him king walks off to live in a cave. Valmiki doesn't rush past it: the city lit up, and two brothers walking away from it into the hills.
screen: `SUGRIVA CROWNED.` → `RAMA WON'T GO IN.` → `TWO BROTHERS WALK TO THE HILLS.`

segments.voice: It's the start of the rainy season. Rama explains: you can't send search parties across the land in the monsoon. Rivers flood, roads vanish. Enjoy your kingdom for these months, he tells Sugriva; when autumn comes, we search. So Rama and Lakshmana go to a mountain called Prasravana and find a wide cave to wait out the rain. Four months, and nothing to do but wait, for a man whose wife is a prisoner somewhere he can't even name. Lakshmana makes it bearable. When Rama sinks into grief, Lakshmana reminds him who he is, and to save his strength for the time to act. And Valmiki fills the chapter with what they see: peaks, rushing water, flowering trees, birds. Hindus still keep these months. They're called chaturmas, the four months. Many traditions say Vishnu goes into his deep sleep on Devshayani Ekadashi, early in the rains, and wakes on Prabodhini Ekadashi in the autumn month of Kartik. Through that season many monks stop wandering and stay in one place, and many households take on a vow: giving up a food, reading a scripture, adding a prayer. Some teachers read Rama's cave as that season in story form: when you can't move, you keep your vow and gather strength. Now the week, by its teachings: dasya, love that serves. Sakhya, friendship sworn before the fire. Touching an elder's feet. A promise given once is kept. Dharma is subtle. Antyeshti, the last rite. And today, chaturmas, and the rain coming in.
screen: `NO SEARCHING IN THE MONSOON.` · `THE CAVE ON PRASRAVANA.` · `CHATURMAS: THE FOUR MONTHS.` · `KEEP A VOW, GATHER STRENGTH.` · then, large: `THE WEEK, AND THE RAIN COMING IN.`

segments.voice: Listen. If there's rain, listen to it; if not, to whatever's there: traffic, a fan, your own breath. Let the sound be the whole practice. If you pray, choose one small vow for this season, the way families do for chaturmas: one food, one page, one prayer. If you don't, choose one small steady habit to keep while you wait for something.
The rains. Sugriva is crowned, and Rama waits out the monsoon in a cave on Prasravana mountain.
Your line: chaturmas, the four holy months of rain. Rama keeps his vow in a cave and waits for autumn. Day five hundred eighty-eight, done.

howItsDone: The four months of the rainy season, chaturmasa, are still kept by some Hindu ascetics and households as a time to stay in one place, travel less, and take on extra vows and study.
